newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says Germany to meet EMU deficit goal in 97.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Germany to meet EMU deficit goal in 97.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday that Germany will meet the Maastricht deficit goal in 1997 despite additional pressure on its budget and that its deficit would be below three percent of GDP in 1998.
In a speech at a banking seminar, Waigel said that despite Bonn's committment to reducing its structural deficit, drastic savings or tax hikes would be counterproductive for growth and employment.
"Germany will meet the criteria for budget deficits of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997, despite the additional pressure on the budget," Waigel said.
The slightly worse-than-forecast German deficit numbers this year would be offset by favourable developments on the social welfare contributions and special funds, Waigel said.
"An undershooting of the deficit reference value is also secured in Germany in 1998," Waigel said.
Current budgetary developments were being strongly influenced by the unfavourable conditions on the labour market, he said.
Bonn would face labour market-related costs from reduced tax revenues and additional spending of about thirty billion marks in 1997, Waigel said.

"Even if we do not deviate from a course of reducing the structural deficit, drastic savings or tax increases would in the current situation have additional counterproductive effects on growth and employment," Waigel said.
